craft_notes: Sthāyin: names-collapse (many names, one supreme). Rows: row 1 (beloved→supreme). Close: supreme (parā as landing, second time: the word insists). Rejected: adding epithets — kept the three names bare (Umā Ramā Sarasvatī uncut); 'please' for favor — kept favor us (prasīda as grace, not politeness).

lines: Favor us, all-blissful Śivā, Śiva's beloved —
Umā, Ramā, Sarasvatī: you, the goddess supreme.
l4.sanskrit_cite: prasīda sarvamaṅgale śive śivasya vallabhe | ume rame sarasvati tvameva devatā parā

reads_against.argmap: Who alone is supreme? → Direct address collapsing names into one: Umā, Ramā, Sarasvatī — you alone the supreme goddess.
c1_essence: Direct address collapsing names into one: Umā, Ramā, Sarasvatī — you alone supreme.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with bhakti (wonder held in devotion)
